hand_reasoning.type: logical_derivation; not presented as executed model evidence
steps: Let n=f(state) be card with the ID key, ask_id without it, address for the address task, and undefined for unsupported tasks. With one correct substantive action and none retained, choose n when n is in the current list; otherwise choose none.

Original and deleted-answer prompts share the exact rules, material and question. Removing only card changes membership and therefore the prescribed label. Missing-ID data instead changes f(state); it is a separate intervention.
The two different preconditions n=card but card absent, and n=undefined, both produce none. Therefore the answer string alone cannot invert this mapping to identify the cause.
If two distinct candidates describe the same needed action, semantic correctness is not unique even when IDs differ; deduplication is a stated dataset condition, not an implemented semantic checker.

Having none present in both members but correct in only one makes the rule always choose none when present inconsistent with this pair. This construction does not prove that any trained model will avoid the shortcut.
Known variants of one scenario are dependent observations; placing variants across train/test cannot establish generalization to unseen scenarios.

limits: No authors PLAN/OUTLINE or any other review/reader/sidecar answer was read.
No model weights, Kev data, model generation, optimizer update, GPU or paid service was used to run these examples. Literal strings and local Python generate the rows.

The program is a toy oracle for well-formed state dictionaries, known unique candidate IDs, and shown lists retaining none. It is not an input validator for empty IDs, unknown IDs, missing task keys or arbitrary absent-none lists.
No learned accuracy, robustness, speed or general model-quality conclusion was tested.
No figure rendering/viewing is claimed: the reviewed lesson has no referenced figures; prerequisite figure layouts were outside this check.
